clue.text: Scenery causing medic to interrupt spinal surgery?

indicators.note: to interrupt means the doctor breaks into the middle of the operation phrase

parts.note: an operation on the back is a BACK OP, op being short for operation
DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor barges into a spinal operation, apparently creating a stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinal surgery' sounds like a description of the procedure; read it literally as a back operation, which 'to interrupt' splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A backdrop is the painted cloth at the rear of a stage, its scenery.

clue.text: Woman's short-range elevation

indicators.note: in a down clue elevation means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top
short means the mountain range loses its final letter

parts.note: the Andes are the great mountain range of South America

explanation.surface: Some woman's limited height above the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts ANDES to ANDE; 'elevation' reads that upwards as EDNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Instrument of state cutting duck up

indicators.note: cutting means the state abbreviation slices into the bird's letters
in a down clue up means the duck is written from bottom to top

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck
NC is the abbreviation for North Carolina, a US state

explanation.surface: A tool of government slicing up a waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a verb or a nation; it is a US state's postal abbreviation, set by 'cutting' into the duck read upwards ('up').
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a small pointed surgical knife, a medical instrument.

clue.text: Mobster and neckwear supremo

parts.note: a scarf is worn round the neck
an ace is an expert, someone supreme at something

explanation.surface: A gangster who is also the leading authority on scarves and ties.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarface was the nickname of Al Capone and the title of gangster films.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface is the famous nickname of the gangster Al Capone, hence a mobster.

clue.text: Senior primate's bag containing French pronoun and another part of speech

indicators.note: containing means the bag holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a sack is a large bag
il is French for he or it
a pronoun is a part of speech, and a verb is another

explanation.surface: A grammar-themed bag belonging to an elderly ape.
explanation.walkthrough: A pronoun is a part of speech, so 'another part of speech' points to a different word class; 'containing' wraps the bag around both.
explanation.definitionFit: A silverback is a mature male gorilla, the senior ape of its troop.

clue.text: What to do before re-dropping provocation?

definitions.meaning: in computer drag-and-drop, you drag an item again before you drop it again
something that enrages, like a cloth waved at a bull

explanation.surface: Advice on what to do before letting something fall again, offered as an incitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-DRAG, the first part is a joke about dragging before dropping again; read as RED RAG it is the cloth that infuriates a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A red rag is proverbially what enrages a bull, so anything sure to provoke anger.

clue.text: Chinese river carrying cold conveyance to Hades?

parts.note: the Han are China's majority ethnic group

indicators.note: carrying means the river holds the cold letter inside it

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, England
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A Chinese river bearing something chilly to the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese river' looks like one unit; it is HAN plus DART, an English river in Devon. 'carrying' puts C in DART.
explanation.definitionFit: Things in decline go to hell in a handcart, so a handcart is the vehicle that carries one to Hades.

clue.text: Academic's dream of ancient letter turning up in note

indicators.note: in means the reversed letter sits inside the musical note

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letter is written bottom to top

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an old Germanic alphabet

explanation.surface: A scholar dreams of an old rune written upside down inside a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the ancient letter from bottom to top; 'in' sets it within the sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is a permanent academic post, the security every lecturer hopes for.

clue.text: What you shouldn't do to a part of Ukraine

parts.note: a crime is something forbidden, something one should not do

explanation.surface: Advice on what not to do to a region of Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link joining CRIME and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea is a peninsula on the Black Sea, internationally regarded as part of Ukraine.

clue.text: Vegetable's all right by artist

parts.note: OK means all right
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A vegetable approved of by a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a green pod eaten as a vegetable, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Dispute with religious recruit swallowing ridiculous rot

indicators.note: swallowing means the recruit takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a convert is someone newly brought into a faith

indicators.note: ridiculous means the word rot is jumbled into a silly order

explanation.surface: An argument with a new believer who has taken in absurd nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' signals the jumble of 'rot', and 'swallowing' puts the jumble inside the recruit after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To controvert is to argue against or deny, so to dispute.

clue.text: What to say when knocking back some pastis or Pernod?

indicators.note: knocking back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about the right toast when downing an aniseed spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' marks TISORP inside 'pastis or Pernod'; 'knocking back' reads it backwards. The clue also reads as a whole: you say the toast when knocking back a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German drinking toast, said as glasses are raised.

clue.text: Bird that is stifling Native American cry

indicators.note: stifling means the two letters smother the people's name between them

parts.note: SC stands for scilicet, Latin for that is to say
the Cree are a Native American people
a howl is a long loud cry

explanation.surface: A bird smothering a Native American's yell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' tempts IE, but here it is SC (Latin scilicet); 'stifling' wraps it round the people, and the cry follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The screech owl is a small owl named for its call.

clue.text: Result of showing 6 to a time-wasting motorist?

definitions.text: Result of showing 6 to a time-wasting motorist?

parts.words: Result of showing 6 to a time-wasting motorist?
parts.note: 6 is a provocation; waving it at a dawdling driver brings on the fury that traffic delays cause

explanation.surface: What happens if you wave a provocation at a slow driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 refers to the answer at 6 down, the proverbial thing that enrages a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is the violent anger of drivers, the result of being provoked on the road.

clue.text: Do one in to get equal status

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the social gathering

parts.note: a do is a party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A party-goer's attempt to gain equal standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but is the noun for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity means equality of rank or standing.

clue.text: Ape going ape during sluttish social event

indicators.note: during means the jumbled letters come within the adjective

parts.note: tarty means tawdry or sluttish

indicators.note: going ape means going wild, so the word ape is scrambled

explanation.surface: A gorilla running wild at a tawdry gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going ape' signals a scramble of the first word, and 'during' sets that jumble inside the adjective just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is an afternoon gathering where tea is served.

clue.text: Male strode around outside, given leave

indicators.note: outside means the reversed walk wraps round the letter for male
around means the word for strode is turned back to front

parts.note: paced means walked with long steps, strode

explanation.surface: A man walked about outdoors once he was allowed time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns PACED into DECAP; 'outside' puts it around M, giving DECA-M-P.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, often secretly.

clue.text: One taking advantage of a below-average location

indicators.note: below means the a goes beneath the average in this down clue

parts.note: par is the normal or average standard
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Someone exploiting a poor spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below-average' reads as poor; split it, so 'below' places the A after the average in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off another, taking advantage of its host.

clue.text: Material for building missile launcher

definitions.meaning: the paste of lime, sand and water that binds bricks
a short gun that lobs shells at a high angle

explanation.definitionFit: Mortar is both bricklayers' binding paste and a high-angle gun firing shells.

clue.text: Muse pursues rocker's foe at a steady pace

indicators.note: pursues means the Muse follows behind the other piece

parts.note: Mods and Rockers were rival British youth gangs of the 1960s
Erato is the Muse of love poetry

explanation.surface: A Muse chases a biker's enemy at a measured speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods (scooter riders in sharp suits) fought Rockers (leather-jacketed motorcyclists) in 1960s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderato is a musical direction meaning at a moderate tempo.

clue.text: Cook goose's heart and another edible organ

indicators.note: heart means the middle letter of the bird's name

parts.note: the heart is an edible organ, and the liver is another

explanation.surface: Prepare a goose's heart along with its liver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like an instruction but is the noun: Jamie Oliver, the TV chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamie Oliver is a famous British television chef, so a cook.

clue.text: Brain-teaser — one among thousands — gains non-English currency

indicators.note: among means the one goes between the two thousands

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, so two Ks are thousands
A means one

indicators.note: non-English means the letter E for English is dropped

parts.note: the euro is a European currency

explanation.surface: A puzzle, one in a thousand, gains popularity abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' looks like popularity; it is the EURO, which loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Kakuro is a Japanese number puzzle, a brain-teaser like sudoku.

clue.text: Family led astray by light

parts.note: kin are one's relatives, family

indicators.note: astray means the word led wanders into a new order

explanation.surface: Relatives are misled by a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a noun but is a verb, as in setting a fire going; 'astray' scrambles 'led'.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle is to light a fire.

clue.text: Demoralise stunner with 10 on organ

indicators.note: on means the number comes after the organ in this across clue

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person, a stunner
the ear is an organ of hearing
ten is the number 10 written out

explanation.surface: Discourage a beauty with a perfect score for hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across; it is simply TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten is to make someone lose heart, to demoralise them.

clue.text: Fuel pipe's opening provides sudden inspiration

parts.note: gas is a fuel

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word pipe

explanation.surface: Opening a fuel pipe gives a burst of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' means breathing in, not a bright idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasp is a sudden sharp intake of breath, a literal inspiration.

clue.text: Musical soldiers

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the plural gives a second GI

explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'soldiers' gives two GIs side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe stage and film musical.

clue.text: Large hole containing backward little bird

indicators.note: containing means the big hole holds the other letters

parts.note: a pit is a large hole in the ground

indicators.note: backward means the word for little is read in reverse

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A big hole holding a shy little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' seems to describe the bird as shy; it reverses the Scottish word for small, which 'containing' places in the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is the lapwing, named for its call.

clue.text: Poem unfinished in class — lower class

indicators.note: in means the shortened poem sits inside the word for class

parts.note: rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

indicators.note: unfinished means the poem loses its last letter

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem

explanation.surface: An incomplete poem in school leads to being sent to a lower class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' appears twice: first as a grade, then within the definition as a rank to be moved down from; 'unfinished' docks the poem, 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to move down to a lower rank or division.
